name: Isolated Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type IIb

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification for Focal Cortical Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of dysmorphic neurons and balloon cells on histopathological examination
MRI evidence of focal cortical thickening, blurring of the gray-white matter junction, and transmantle sign
Focal epilepsy refractory to medical treatment with seizure semiology consistent with cortical localization
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing focal epileptiform discharges correlating with lesion location

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of dysmorphic neurons and balloon cells plus MRI findings consistent with FCD IIb and clinical evidence of focal epilepsy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation; MRI and clinical features guide pre-surgical evaluation.

pathognomonic.notes: Seizures typically begin in childhood or adolescence

pathognomonic.symptomName: Seizure semiology consistent with cortical origin
searchTerms: seizure symptoms matching brain cortex origin
seizure signs consistent with cortical source

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of balloon cells on histopathology
pathognomonic.notes: Pathognomonic cellular feature of type IIb
searchTerms: presence of abnormal balloon-shaped brain cells
balloon cells seen on brain pathology
large abnormal cells in brain tissue
temporary weakness on one side after seizure
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

imaging: MRI showing cortical thickening, blurring of gray-white matter junction, and transmantle sign
FDG-PET hypometabolism in affected cortical region
other: Histopathology revealing dysmorphic neurons and balloon cells

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement with skin, renal, and cardiac lesions
Presence of cortical tubers rather than isolated focal dysplasia
Genetic mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 genes
Presence of a well-demarcated tumor on imaging
Typically associated with seizures but distinct pathology

redFlags: Onset of focal seizures in early childhood refractory to multiple antiepileptic drugs
MRI evidence of cortical abnormalities with transmantle sign
references: Blumcke I, et al. The clinicopathologic spectrum of focal cortical dysplasias: a consensus classification. Epilepsia. 2011 Jun;52(6):158-174.
Wang Y, et al. Somatic mutations in MTOR cause focal cortical dysplasia type IIb. Nat Genet. 2016;48(4):395-400.
International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification of Focal Cortical Dysplasia, 2011.
